incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH LATENCY: route=text-generate in us-west-2 — p50/p95 exceeded SLOs. Auto-page: sarah (oncall) at 1807001234.
sarah (oncall): I see the synthetic checks spiking since ~1807001000. Dashboard: p50 ~180ms (was ~60ms), p95 ~820ms (was ~200ms). No error-rate increase. Customers report intermittent slowness.
mike (eng-runtime): looking into traces now. Any recent deploys?
dan (eng-platform): we had a kernel & distro security update rolled to canary nodes at 1806999000 and to 40% of prod at 1807000200. No app-level deploys since last week.
jess (eng-sre): copying quick status: CPU and mem look normal on hosts, but I see rcu stall warnings on two hosts. Also increased context-switch rate. Going to pull `dmesg` and perf counters.
olga (eng-ml): model-side metrics show stable token compute. KV cache hit rate slightly lower (~2-3% change). Not enough to explain 4x p95.
kevin (customer-ops): fielding two inbound tickets from enterprise customers in us-west with reports of slow responses. They're asking for immediate mitigation options.
sarah (oncall): mitigation: (1) enable fallback to smaller model variant for affected route, (2) enable extra capacity on dedicated pool, (3) pin traffic to unaffected AZ if possible. Mike — can you toggle model fallback? Dan — can you scale capacity?
mike (eng-runtime): I can enable fallback in the routing policy; flipping now to route 10% -> model-x-small, 90% -> model-x. Doing a canary redirect in 30s.
incident-bot: routing change applied by mike at 1807001302 — 10% fallback enabled.
jess (eng-sre): added a temporary CPU governor change on two noisy hosts to performance to avoid freq-scaling thrash.
dan (eng-platform): scaled inference pool +30% (added 6 instances) at 1807001330. Autoscaler still respecting burst cap.
kevin (customer-ops): letting customers know now. Posting interim note: "We're aware of increased latency for some requests in us-west-2. Our engineers are actively investigating and have applied mitigations; we'll update in 15m."
mike (eng-runtime): initial trace sample: gRPC handler timing increased inside `accept_token()` span. Most time in syscalls around socket recv and epoll_wait. Example spans: `grpc_recv -> accept_token (kernel_wait) -> kv_lookup` where kernel_wait jumped from 2ms to 150ms for p95.

Shared trace snippet (summarized):
```
trace_id=abcd1234 span=gRPC_recv  exec_time=820ms
  span=accept_token exec_time=740ms
    span=kernel_wait exec_time=720ms
    span=kv_lookup exec_time=10ms
```

jess (eng-sre): pulled perf counters on an affected host (host-12):
```
# perf stat -a -e context-switches,cpu-migrations,page-faults,cycles,instructions -- sleep 10
 Performance counter stats for 'system wide':
   1,254,321 context-switches  # huge compared to baseline ~120k
     12,342 cpu-migrations
    45,678 page-faults
  2,345,000,000 cycles
  4,567,000,000 instructions
```

jess (eng-sre): also `dmesg` shows network driver NAPI warnings on host-12 and host-17 around the same time as the kernel update.
mike (eng-runtime): correlating node list to latency hot hosts: host-12, host-17, host-19 show the worst p95s. All three were included in the rolling kernel update batch at 1807000200.

Hypothesis tracking (in-thread):
- H1: Kernel/security update introduced a regression in NIC driver or scheduler causing high kernel wait/softirq delays -> observable as increased kernel_wait span.
- H2: Runtime change (unlikely) — no app deploys.
- H3: Network congestion in AZ — but infra network metrics not showing increased retransmits.

olga (eng-ml): can we get a CPU-steal / irqbalance / softirq histogram from the hosts? If softirq/steal high, hints toward driver/interrupt handling issue.
jess (eng-sre): collecting `cat /proc/interrupts` and `sar -I SUM` now. Dumping snippets: 
```
# /proc/interrupts (host-12)
  CPU0       CPU1       CPU2       CPU3
  45:    12345678   23456789   34567890   45678901  IR-IO-APIC  eth0
  46:    12345000   23456000   34567000   45678000  IR-IO-APIC  eth1
```

jess (eng-sre): `sar -I SUM` shows softirq time jumped from 0.2% -> 6% at 1807000205 across affected hosts.
mike (eng-runtime): tracing confirms spots where epoll_wait returns after long kernel scheduling delay. Also seeing higher number of futex wait times in perf. Could be contention in shared resources.

sarah (oncall): next steps:
- immediate: continue fallback and scale until p95 drops under 350ms.
- mid term: isolate impacted nodes from rotation and rollback kernel update on canary if we can reproduce.
- long term: full RCA and postmortem.

mike (eng-runtime): I'm going to remove the affected hosts from rotation (host-12/17/19) at 1807001385. Marking them DRAIN so no new sessions.

incident-bot: host-12 removed from rotation by mike at 1807001387. host-17/19 pending.
jess (eng-sre): rolling kernel rollback plan: revert package to prior kernel-5.15.x on the 3 affected hosts in rotation with quick validation. Need platform approval to expedite.
dan (eng-platform): approving rollback for the 3 nodes. I'll coordinate with infra to push the rollback and reboot. ETA 10-15m.

kevin (customer-ops): customers acknowledged mitigation note; one asked for postmortem. I'll collect impacted customer list and SLAs in parallel.

[~15 minutes later]
mike (eng-runtime): after draining and scaling, p50 dropped to 70ms, p95 to ~240ms. Good improvement but still above baseline p95 200ms.
jess (eng-sre): kernel rollback initiated on host-12 at 1807001430; host-12 shows decreased softirq and context-switch counts after reboot. Host-12 p95 returned to ~210ms.

olga (eng-ml): model perf stable; good signal this is infra-level.

mike (eng-runtime): reproduced locally on an internal repro cluster by upgrading kernel to the same package — saw the same epoll/futex stalls in `strace` and `perf`. Filing a kernel bug report and will attach `perf.data` + strace logs.

sarah (oncall): good work. For the in-incident RCA notes: root-cause hypothesis currently: regression in kernel/network stack after recent kernel package update leading to increased softirq and scheduling latency, which inflates kernel_wait spans in gRPC handlers and drives p95 latency regression.

Action items (tracked here):
1) mike: attach trace + perf data to the bug report and include host IDs and kernel package version (doing).
2) jess/dan: complete rollback for remaining affected hosts and validate.
3) dan: hold kernel rollouts until patch validated in canary.
4) olga: validate model correctness under fallback once more (complete).
5) kevin: compile impacted customer list + communications for postmortem.

mike (eng-runtime): attaching quick commands used: 
```
# collect perf
sudo perf record -a -g -F 99 -o /tmp/perf.data sleep 30
sudo perf script -i /tmp/perf.data > /tmp/perf.out

# strace on process
sudo strace -tt -f -p <pid> -o /tmp/strace.log
```

jess (eng-sre): final status update: mitigations in place, rollback completed for 3 hosts, scaling + fallback reduced customer impact. We're keeping the incident open for RCA documentation.
sarah (oncall): handoff to night oncall @jess at 1807001450 — I'll update the incident channel with the runbook and the list of artifacts attached to the bug. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
jess (eng-sre): acknowledged — will continue monitoring, and will prepare a short incident write-up for the postmortem queue.
incident-bot: Incident status changed to INVESTIGATING -> MITIGATED by sarah at 1807001450.
